.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

No significant changes made.

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 222 AM EDT Saturday...

1. Generally cool weather is expected over the next several 
days. Sunday will be briefly warmer, but a front will cross on 
Monday bringing gusty winds, showers, and a return to the cooler 
weather.

2. Cold air mid week will moderate by the late week with a 
pattern change for the weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 222 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A broad 1028mb surface high will be positioned to our 
west over the Great Lakes region today. This will keep northerly 
flow across the region. Fortunately, the cool air coming in will be 
more of a glancing blow with zonal flow aloft. Still, it'll feel 
plenty cool with highs lingering mainly in the 50s, except for a few 
60s across south-central Vermont. Mountain summits will likely be in 
the upper 30s to mid 40s this afternoon. Abundant dry air will 
promote clear skies. We should radiate quite efficiently tonight 
with these conditions, and that will bring overnight lows in the 30-
40 F range.

High pressure will start moving east Sunday, and south to southwest 
winds return. A more moderate day in the 60s is expected for Sunday, 
with a warmer night around 40-50 F. These warmer conditions will 
come with some wind, though as pressure gradients tighten against 
departing high pressure and the next approaching system. Anticipate 
10-15 mph winds, and up to 20 mph in the Champlain Valley. The 
attendant frontal boundary will arrive pre-dawn through the early 
afternoon. The moisture is not great, but the dynamics of a strong 
upper jet and modest frontal support could produce a broken narrow 
line of rain. Larger synoptic scale motion will yield stronger winds 
behind this front. Combined with the strength of cold air behind it, 
the 50s forecast on Monday and 25-35 mph gusts across the region 
will feel nippy. Advective cold will result in mid 20s to upper 30s. 
The winds may still preclude frost formation in the Champlain 
Valley, but plenty cool. Moisture quickly departs behind the frontal 
boundary, but if there's anything lingering, a few flakes or some 
riming is feasible for mountain terrain.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Strong northwest flow will continue through Tuesday with 
temperatures feeling solidly like fall, before our air mass 
moderates towards the weekend. Highs Tuesday will struggle to reach 
50 in the higher terrain with low to mid 50s elsewhere with breezy 
northwest winds as our flow pattern remains fairly confluent. Skies 
will remain clear into Tuesday night with one of the coldest nights 
of the season expected. With a stout dry 700-500mb layer, strong 
radiational cooling will take place with many places falling into 
the low to mid 30s. Some patchy frost will be possible in the 
sheltered locations, but with temperatures falling under clear 
skies, almost the entire region could experience a freeze, with the 
Champlain valley remaining on alert at this time. This will likely 
be a curtain call for gardeners sensitive plants in the broad 
valleys. 

Temperatures will slowly moderate back up towards the weekend with 
the approach of a broad long wave trough associated with a deepening 
upper low over the Hudson Bay. Highs will warm to the upper 50s to 
mid 60s, with overnight lows in the upper 30s to mid 40s. A large 
scale cyclonic gyre will shift south from the interior of Canada 
leading to several shortwave passages beginning late next week into 
the weekend. Daily diurnally enhanced showers will be possible 
starting Thursday with increasing cloud cover into the weekend. In 
addition to increasing shower chances, each shortwave passage will 
bring with it some breezy to gusty winds to northern New York, and 
likely some channeled flow in the Champlain Valley each day.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 06Z Sunday...A clearing cold front is currently pushing
through the region from the northwest, with a mix of terminal
conditions ahead of the front. Across Vermont, where the front is
just approaching, antecedent valley fog is leading to MVFR-IFR
visibility and cig reductions at EFK/RUT/MPV. In northern New York,
mixing and the presence of a modest LLJ, behind the front, are
helping scour out any fog at least for the next few hours. The LLJ
may lead to some brief LLWS with 20- 30 knot winds associated with
front axis. As the front moves through Vermont over the next few
hours, expectations are that mixing and prevailing flow aloft should
trend fog chances down with general improving terminal conditions
towards VFR. Have used TEMPO groups at MPV/EFK to denote when fog
should mix out with conditions improving towards VFR. RUT will
likely see VCFG through 08Z, though confidence in the prevailing fog
is low. As sites rebound to VFR by 09-10Z, some decoupling towards
sunrise may lead to brief additional fog at SLK, though confidence
is low with a only a TEMPO used. Beyond 12Z, all terminals are
expected to return to VFR with calmer and quiet conditions. Light
north winds 10 knots or less are expected through the daylight
hours. Winds will trend calm after sunset tonight with fog expected
at the climo favored terminals beyond 04Z.
